name: Career change
description: Move into a new field: clarify the target role, close the skill gaps, build proof of your work and run a structured job search with interview practice.

steps.title: Define the target role and why
steps.description: Research roles in the new field: day-to-day work, salary range, entry paths. Choose one or two target roles and write down why they fit you.

steps.title: Skill-gap analysis
steps.description: Collect about ten job postings for the target role, list the skills they ask for and mark what you already have, what is partial and what is missing.

steps.title: Talk to people already in the field
steps.description: Have at least five short conversations. Ask what the job is really like, what they would learn first and who is hiring.

steps.title: Learning plan for the top three gaps
steps.description: Pick the three gaps that appear most often and choose one course or book for each. Study them in order of importance.

steps.title: Portfolio project 1
steps.description: Build something that solves a real problem in the target field. Document the problem, your decisions and the result.

steps.title: Portfolio project 2
steps.description: A second, different project that shows range. Reuse what you learned and aim for something finished over something big.

steps.title: Rewrite your CV, profile and personal story
steps.description: Reframe your past experience for the new role. Write a one-page CV, an updated online profile and a two-minute story of why you are changing.

steps.title: Build your network and visibility
steps.description: Join communities, attend events, share what you are learning and message people who work where you would like to work.

steps.title: Interview preparation
steps.description: Prepare stories for behavioural questions, review the technical topics of the role and research each company before each interview.

steps.title: Mock interviews with feedback
steps.description: Practise with a friend, mentor or recording. Ask for honest feedback on clarity, structure and confidence.

steps.title: Run the job search
steps.description: Apply in batches, tailor each application, follow up after a week and keep a tracker with dates, contacts and next steps.

steps.title: Negotiate and decide
steps.description: Compare offers on more than salary: growth, learning, team and stability. Negotiate calmly with market data.

competencies.name: Role-specific skills
competencies.description: The technical or professional skills the target role requires day to day.

competencies.name: Portfolio evidence
competencies.description: Finished work that proves you can do the job.

competencies.name: Interviewing
competencies.description: Answer questions clearly with structured examples and ask good questions back.

competencies.name: Networking
competencies.description: Build relationships with people in the new field who can advise or refer you.

competencies.name: Personal narrative
competencies.description: Explain in a convincing way why you are changing and what you bring from before.

cards.front: What does STAR stand for in interview answers?
cards.back: Situation, Task, Action, Result. Set the scene briefly, say what you had to do, explain what you did and finish with the measurable outcome.

cards.front: How should you structure 'Tell me about yourself'?
cards.back: Present, past, future in under two minutes: what you do now, the experience that led here and why this role is the next step.

cards.front: How do you answer 'What is your biggest weakness?'
cards.back: Name a real, minor weakness, show what you are doing about it and give a recent example of improvement.

cards.front: Who should name the salary number first?
cards.back: Ideally the employer. Research the market range beforehand and, if asked first, answer with a range based on data, not on your last salary.

cards.front: What belongs in a portfolio project write-up?
cards.back: The problem, your role, the approach and decisions, the result, what you would improve, and a link to a demo or the code.

cards.front: Formula for a strong CV bullet
cards.back: Action verb + what you did + measurable result, for example: Reduced report preparation time by 40% by automating the monthly export.

cards.front: What do you ask in an informational interview?
cards.back: What a normal week looks like, what they wish they had known at the start, which skills matter most and who else you should talk to.

cards.front: Good questions to ask at the end of an interview
cards.back: What does success look like in the first six months? How is the team organised? What is the biggest challenge right now?
